body:
# Independent audit: a full triangular zero endpoint closes this cap regime


proved positive-part cover lemma, actual captured-facet extrusion, and
the stated actual three-fiber cap configuration. Neither mixed OC nor
an equivalent unproved center theorem is invoked.

Let A,K,B be full planar fibers at -1,0,1, with (A+B)/2 contained in K,
0 in int K, and

    B=T={x<=1,y<=1,-x-y<=1},    b=|B|=9/2.

Suppose the three caps H_i={v_i.x>=z}, with
v_1=(1,0),v_2=(0,1),v_3=(-1,-1), all attain the actual raw mixed
depth Q of the source (0,0). Assume every A cut is proper. All B
captures are supporting facets and have zero area. Put a=|A|,
k=|K|, M=a+k+b. Relabel the A captured areas as u<=v<=w, retaining
which normal corresponds to each, and set

    F=u+v+w/4,   delta=a-u-v.

The conclusion is that some actual mixed-integer point has normalized
depth at least 2/9. If b<=a+k, the source itself has this guarantee.
If b>a+k, the ordinary centroid in the B fiber supplies it.

## 1. The two ordinary cap-cover profiles

The positive-part ordinary cover lemma, proved by sequential parallel
trimming in `candidate 64b80eee72258d21`,
says that a planar convex body L covered by caps of areas c_i satisfies

    |L|<=sum_i(c_i-alpha)_+ +(9/4)alpha              (1)

for every alpha>=0. This follows from the ordinary planar Grünbaum
constant 4/9, and handles closed caps exactly because all these traces
have nonzero continuous normals.

The middle traces cover the entire plane: their normals sum to zero.
Their areas are Q-u,Q-v,Q-w, and each is positive because the source
is interior to K. Set alpha=Q-w in (1). Exact cancellation gives

    k<=(9/4)Q-F.                                   (2)

The A traces also cover the entire plane, since their thresholds are
all -1 and at least one of the three normal values is nonnegative at
every point. Set alpha=u in (1) for A. This gives

    a<=w+v+u/4,
    delta<=w-3u/4<=w.                              (3)

No projected integral has replaced a fiber sum, and these are ordinary
area statements on their actual single fibers.

## 2. The deficit corner forces a long captured extrusion

If F<a, then delta>w/4>=0. In particular u+v<a, so the two smaller
A caps miss a set of strictly positive A-area simultaneously. Every
point in that strict missed set satisfies

    v_i.x<-1, v_j.x<-1,

where i,j index the two smaller caps. Because v_k=-v_i-v_j, the
remaining normal, whose A captured area is w, satisfies v_k.x>2
there. Thus h_k=max_A v_k.x>2.

The complete B facet for that normal has length 3||v_k||. Properness
of the A cut gives the captured A normal width (h_k+1)/||v_k||.
The actual set (A_k+B_facet)/2 is inside the captured K cap. Planar
segment extrusion has exact area

    |A_k+B_facet|=w+3(h_k+1).

This identity and all orientations/status restrictions are proved in
`candidate 78ddd5dbdcb0b0a1`.
Consequently

    Q=w+q_k >= [5w+3(h_k+1)]/4
                 >9/4+5w/4.                       (4)

This is the key strict charge: the zero-area B capture cannot be
discarded because its actual facet produces positive middle area.

## 3. A direct quantitative split

Assume first b<=a+k. If F>=a, (2) gives

    M<=b+(9/4)Q,
    b<=a+k<=(9/4)Q.

Hence M<=(9/2)Q and Q/M>=2/9.

If F<a, combine (2) and (3) to obtain

    M<=b+delta-w/4+(9/4)Q
       <=9/2+3w/4+(9/4)Q.                         (5)

Using (4), the ratio Q/M is strictly greater than

    (9/4+5w/4) /
      [(9/4)(9/4+5w/4)+9/2+3w/4].

This is increasing for w>=0: after writing its numerator as
A+Bw and its denominator as C+Dw, its derivative has the sign of
BC-AD=63/16>0. Its value at w=0 is 4/17. Thus this whole deficit
branch has the stronger strict conclusion

    Q/M>4/17>2/9.                                 (6)

No nonheavy assumption is needed for the derivation of (6) itself.
If B is heavy instead, its actual centroid has raw depth at least
(4/9)b>(2/9)M from its own B contribution alone.

The source conclusion controls EVERY ambient halfspace because Q is
assumed to be the actual attained source depth. A family of candidate
caps of mass Q that are only locally minimizing does not justify that
last inference. This distinction is retained throughout the audit.

## 4. Equivalent contradiction calculation checked independently

If one assumes Q<(2/9)M, (2) implies

    k<a+b-2F,
    Q<(4/9)(a+b-F).

Under b<=a+k, the first forces F<a. By (3), the second then gives

    Q<2+w/3.

This contradicts (4), with exact positive gap

    (9/4+5w/4)-(2+w/3)=1/4+11w/12.

Only B's nonheaviness is needed here. No nonheavy assumption on A
or K, section-capacity inequality, source-chord centroid condition,
or ordinary global homothety is silently used.

## 5. Exact frontier for a partial zero-endpoint facet

Keep the normalized circuit and a convex endpoint B subset T with
positive area b, but suppose its actual facet in the largest-A-cap
direction has length ell_k||v_k||. The same proof in the F<a branch
gives

    Q>(5w+3ell_k)/4,
    M<=(9/4)Q+b+3w/4.                              (7)

Therefore the branch already implies Q/M>=2/9 whenever

    27ell_k+33w>=16b.                              (8)

In particular either ell_k>=16b/27 or w>=16b/33 suffices. Conversely
a sub-OC configuration of this cap type must have

    27ell_k+33w<16b,
    w<16b/33,
    a<=9w/4<12b/11.                               (9)

The inequality a<=9w/4 follows from (1) with alpha=w. These are
necessary restrictions, not a proof for arbitrary partial facets.
The actual short facet must not be filled to the enclosing T facet;
doing so would invalidate (7). No uniform ordinary-depth surplus of
B is inferred from its short facet.

## 6. Global integer-tilt equalization strengthens the remaining frontier

Use the finite-tilt equalization lemma proved in Section 6 of
`candidate fee4b98d94ecbcf2`.
Its short proof in the present situation is as follows. Keep the
continuous normal and the middle threshold fixed. As the integer
tilt varies from one extreme to the other, the endpoint captured
volumes vary continuously from (a,0) to (0,b). They therefore agree
at some value t,t. Their actual midpoint lies in the same middle cap,
so ordinary BM gives q>=t. If the original cap is globally minimizing
over these integer tilts and had endpoint captures w,0, then 2t>=w.
Consequently

    q>=w/2,   Q=w+q>=3w/2.                         (10)

No endpoint properness at the equalizing tilt is assumed. Nonempty
positive equal captures hold here because w>0, and boundary caps
have zero planar area. This is a statement about all tilts with the
normal fixed; local normal stationarity alone cannot supply it.

For a genuinely sub-OC configuration with B nonheavy, Section 4's
profile bound is Q<4b/9+w/3. Combining with (10) yields

    w<8b/21,
    a<=9w/4<6b/7.                                 (11)

Thus every still-unclosed partial-facet configuration has a strictly
smaller A fiber, by this explicit factor. The simultaneous necessary
facet frontier (9) remains valid. For a weak assumed upper bound
Q<=(2/9)M, these mass-ratio conclusions become w<=8b/21 and
a<=6b/7; all other strictness must be tracked separately. B's
nonheaviness is the only nonheavy premise used in this derivation.
If B is heavy, its ordinary centroid already supplies the OC bound.
